Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
The data point to around August 2018. The fed funds rate is about 2.18%, the 2-year yield is 2.83% and the 10-year is 3.06%, which fits mid-2018. Unemployment is 3.9%, which fits May–August 2018 (it was 3.8% in May and 3.9% in June). Core CPI at 2.19% year over year is slightly low for mid-2018, since core CPI was about 2.2% in August 2018. Headline CPI at 2.68% fits August 2018, when it was 2.7%.

Other readings are consistent with that date:
- Fed funds averaged 1.91% in August 2018 and 2.18% in September 2018. The policy rate rose 0.27 over three months, from about 1.91% to 2.18%, which suggests September 2018 (the 3-month-earlier value would be June, about 1.91%).
- Unemployment in September 2018 was 3.7%, but a 3.9% reading with a 12-month change of -0.5 puts it at 3.9% in August 2017... no, the 12-month change of -0.5 from 4.4% is a better match for 2018. Unemployment was 4.4% in about Sept 2017 and 4.4% in Aug 2017, so the 3.9% reading fits mid-2018 data (June 2018).
- Gold is down 11% over 6 months, and the 10-year yield is at 3.06%. The 2-year yield is 2.83% and the 10-year is 3.06% in a month when the 10-year was falling, which fits August 2018 (10y 2.86%) less well. Late-September 2018 had a 10-year yield of about 3.06%, and the 2-year about 2.82%.

So I settle on September 2018. The VIX of 12.41 is a bit low for that month, but the VIX was low in late September.
